To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lymph node count and node density are independent predictors of disease-specific survival after radical inguinal lymphadenectomy for patients with penile cancer.

(1) lymph node count is the most important predictor of disease-specific survival after radical pelvic lymphadenectomy for patients with penile cancer, and that (2) lymph node density is a better predictor of survival than lymph node count alone, especially for patients with low lymph node count.
